census.help: this button also has an action to zoom the window
Control bar. Contains buttons and displays for key project and app functions. To customize, Control-click the control bar and choose Customize Control Bar and Display.
Display Mode, Display Mode pop-up menu. Switch the ruler display between bars and beats, or hours, minutes, and seconds, or a combination of both. You can also open giant displays.
census.title: Beats & Project

census.help: Playhead Position (Bars), Playhead Position display. Indicates the playhead position in bars and beats. Drag each element vertically to edit it, or double-click and enter a new value.
Tempo, Tempo display. Indicates the playback or recording speed. Drag vertically to speed up or slow down the tempo, or double-click and enter a new value.

Project Tempo menu, Project Tempo pop-up menu. Choose whether the project tempo is maintained, adapts to the tempo of audio recordings and imported audio files, or if Logic Pro determines the project tempo behavior.
Time Signature, Time Signature display. Indicates the number of beats in a bar and the note value for one beat. Drag vertically to edit the value, or double-click and enter a new value.
Key Signature, Key Signature display. Indicates the key signature of the project. Choose a major or minor key signature from the pop-up menu.
Cycle   C, Cycle button. Use Cycle to repeatedly play, or record over, the project section within the yellow cycle area that appears in the ruler.
census.title: Cycle

census.help: Flashback Capture   ⇧R, Flashback Capture. Capture a recent MIDI or audio performance, even if Logic Pro wasn’t recording while you were playing.
census.title: Flashback Capture

census.help: Free Tempo Recording   ⌃⌥⌘R, Free Tempo Recording. Mutes all existing content during recording and performs a Smart Tempo analysis.
census.title: Free Tempo Recording

census.help: Record   R, Record button. Record to the selected track, or to multiple record-ready tracks.
census.title: Record

census.help: Play   ⌅, Play button. Start playback from the playhead position, or from the left locator shown in the ruler when in Cycle mode.
census.title: Play

census.help: Go to Beginning   ↩, Go to Beginning button. Move the playhead to the start of the project.
census.title: Go to Beginning

census.help: Replace   /, Replace button. Replace an existing recording, or a portion of it, with a new recording.
census.title: Replace

census.help: Tuner, Tuner button. Tune instruments connected to your system.
census.title: Tuner

census.help: Solo, Solo button. Only hear selected regions during playback.
census.title: Solo

census.help: Count In   ⇧K, Count-in button. Play a predefined count-in before recording starts. Control-click the button to open a menu where you can choose the count-in length.
census.title: Count In

census.help: Metronome Click   ⌃⇧R, Metronome button. Hear a click at the project tempo during playback or recording. Click and hold for further options.
census.title: Metronome Click

census.help: Library   Y, Library button. Load patches and presets for the selected channel strip or plug-in type; start playing immediately. Loading a patch can affect multiple channel strips.
census.title: Library

census.help: Inspector   I, Inspector button. View and edit region and track settings, based on where you’re working and the item selected. You can also set channel strip pan and volume, or add effects.
census.title: Inspector

census.help: Quick Help button. Show the Quick Help area. If the inspector is closed, Quick Help opens as a separate window.
census.title: Quick Help

census.help: Toolbar   ⌃⌥⌘T, Toolbar button. Show the toolbar, which contains buttons for key functions.
census.title: Toolbar

census.help: Smart Controls   B, Smart Controls button. Quickly modify the sound of the current patch without having to edit individual channel strips or plug-ins.
census.title: Smart Controls

census.help: Mixer   X, Mixer button. Open the Mixer, which shows channel strips for each track in the project. You can edit channel strip controls, add and edit plug-ins, and customize routing options.
census.title: Mixer

census.help: Editors   E, Editors button. Access editors—Audio Track, Audio File, Session Players, Piano Roll, Score, or Step Editor—based on the selected track type.
census.title: Editors

census.help: List Editors   D, List Editors button. View and edit MIDI events, markers, tempo changes, and signature events.
census.title: List Editors

census.help: Note Pads   ⌃⇧P, Note Pads button. Create, view, and edit project and track text notes.
census.title: Note Pads

census.help: Loop Browser   O, Loop Browser button. Add prerecorded loops to your project.
census.title: Loop Browser

census.help: Browsers   F, Browsers button. Access audio and other media files. You can also import data and settings from other projects.
census.title: Browsers

census.help: Left inspector channel strip. Control the signal of the selected track without having to open the Mixer.
Name field. Double-click to rename the channel strip.
Mute button. Silence a channel strip so it’s no longer audible. Use on an aux or output channel strip to silence that part of the mix, or on the master channel strip to mute the project.
Solo button. Isolate a channel strip’s signal so that it can be heard alone. Use on an aux or output channel strip to isolate that part of the mix.
Record Enable button. Prepare the track for recording, or deactivate a record-ready track. The button changes to indicate whether the track is inactive, record enabled, or currently recording.
Input Monitoring button. Hear incoming signals on audio or software instrument tracks that aren’t record enabled. This is useful when setting levels or practicing parts before recording.

Volume fader. Set a track’s playback volume. Use on an aux or output channel strip to adjust the volume of that part of the mix. You can leave the Volume fader of the master channel strip at 0 dB in most cases.

Volume display. Shows the position of the Volume fader referenced to the dB scale to the left of the Mixer. Positive values increase the signal level, negative values decrease it, and 0 dB leaves it unchanged.
census.title: volume fader level, 0.0 dB

census.help: Peak Level display. Shows the signal peak during playback. Values above 0 dB turn red to indicate signal clipping. Orange values above 0 dB do not clip due to internal floating point calculations.
census.title: peak level meter

Channel Mode button. Click to switch the channel strip input format between Mono and Stereo. Long-click, then choose Mono, Stereo, Left, Right, or Surround from the pop-up menu.

Input slot. Choose the channel strip input source. This can be an input of your audio device (your microphone or instrument is connected to) or an internal bus (to receive a signal from another channel strip).

EQ display. Click to add a Channel EQ or open an inserted Channel or Linear Phase EQ. Shift-click to add a Linear Phase EQ. Use EQ to shape an audio signal by adjusting the levels of specific frequency ranges.
Gain reduction meter. Shows the gain reduction of the first Compressor plug-in. If no Compressor is inserted, it shows the gain reduction of an inserted Limiter or Adaptive Limiter plug-in.
Setting button. Load and save channel strip settings, which contain setup information for a channel strip, including plug-ins.
Name field. Double-click to rename the channel strip.
Mute button. Silence a channel strip so it’s no longer audible. Use on an aux or output channel strip to silence that part of the mix, or on the master channel strip to mute the project.
Solo button. Isolate a channel strip’s signal so that it can be heard alone. Use on an aux or output channel strip to isolate that part of the mix.

Volume fader. Set a track’s playback volume. Use on an aux or output channel strip to adjust the volume of that part of the mix. You can leave the Volume fader of the master channel strip at 0 dB in most cases.

Volume display. Shows the position of the Volume fader referenced to the dB scale to the left of the Mixer. Positive values increase the signal level, negative values decrease it, and 0 dB leaves it unchanged.
census.title: volume fader level, 0.0 dB

census.help: Peak Level display. Shows the signal peak during playback. Values above 0 dB turn red to indicate signal clipping. Orange values above 0 dB do not clip due to internal floating point calculations.
census.title: peak level meter

census.help: Pan/Balance knob. Drag vertically to position the channel strip signal in the stereo field.
Group slot. Add the channel strip to a group. You can also define which channel strip controls can be edited for the entire group at the same time.
